About This Document

Executive Summary

What is OmniPilot Hardware?
OmniPilot began as a voice-first AI assistant — a personal copilot that lives on your phone and helps you navigate digital life through conversation. Now we are extending that intelligence into the physical world through purpose-built hardware devices that solve real, urgent problems for underserved populations in India.

This document presents a comprehensive business plan for OmniPilot Hardware — three interconnected hardware verticals that leverage our existing AI voice platform to create affordable, accessible devices for the Indian market.

The Three Verticals

VerticalWhat It IsTarget PriceAddressable Market
Blind Assistive AICamera pendant that describes the world in Hindi via AIRs 4,999 – Rs 24,99960M+ visually impaired Indians
Drone Voice ControlSDK + hardware adapter for voice-controlled dronesRs 8,999 SDK licenseRs 12,000 Cr drone market by 2030
BLE PendantAlways-listening AI companion pendant (Omi competitor)Rs 2,499 – Rs 4,99910M+ tech-savvy Indian consumers

Why This Matters

India has the largest population of visually impaired people in the world — over 60 million. The cheapest assistive AI device today costs Rs 28,000 (Seekr). Our device costs Rs 4,999. The government's ADIP scheme can make it free for eligible users. No one else has built this for India, in Indian languages, at Indian prices.

The Core Thesis: AI hardware doesn't need to be expensive. By combining commodity hardware (Rs 1,500 camera module + Rs 800 processor) with cloud AI (Rs 3/day operating cost), we can build devices that were impossible 3 years ago. India's manufacturing ecosystem (VVDN, Dixon) and government schemes (ADIP, BIRAC) create a unique window to build and scale these devices from India, for India.

Phase 1 — Strategy

1.1 The Hardware Vision

The Evolution: Think of how Google went from search (software) to Pixel phones and Nest cameras (hardware). OmniPilot is making the same leap — from a voice AI app on your phone to purpose-built devices that bring AI into the physical world. The voice assistant is the brain; hardware gives it eyes, ears, and hands.

OmniPilot's hardware strategy is built on a simple insight: the same AI pipeline that powers our voice assistant can power specialized hardware devices. Our speech-to-text, intent recognition, and text-to-speech stack already works. The question is: what physical problems can we solve by giving that AI stack sensors and actuators?

Why Hardware, Why Now?

Three converging trends make 2026 the right time for OmniPilot to enter hardware:

  1. AI model costs have collapsed. Running YOLOv8 on a $15 processor was impossible in 2023. Today, the Allwinner V851s runs object detection at 30fps for $4. Cloud inference via API costs Rs 0.01/query.
  2. India's hardware ecosystem has matured. Contract manufacturers like VVDN and Dixon can produce 5,000-unit runs profitably. PCB fabrication that required Shenzhen in 2020 now happens in Noida and Pune at competitive prices.
  3. Government schemes create free distribution. The ADIP scheme (Assistance to Disabled Persons) reimburses Rs 10,000+ per assistive device. BIRAC offers Rs 50L grants for health-tech innovation. These aren't theoretical — they're active funding channels.
Strategic Insight: We're not building a hardware company from scratch. We're extending an existing AI platform into hardware form factors. The AI pipeline is built. The voice interface is built. We just need to give it new sensors (camera, depth, mic array) and new outputs (spatial audio, haptic feedback, MAVLink commands).

Prioritization Rationale

Blind Assistive is Priority #1 despite the pendant being technically simpler. Reason: social impact creates media coverage, government funding eligibility (ADIP, BIRAC), and a defensible market position. The pendant is Priority #2 for revenue. Drone voice control is Priority #3 for scale.

1.3 Blind Assistive — The #1 Priority

Why Blind Assistive First — 6 Reasons:
  1. Massive unmet need: 60M+ visually impaired Indians, near-zero have AI assistive devices
  2. Price gap: Cheapest competitor (Seekr) is Rs 28,000. Our target is Rs 4,999. That's 5.6x cheaper.
  3. Government funding: ADIP scheme reimburses up to Rs 10,000/device. BIRAC grants up to Rs 50L for development.
  4. Language advantage: No competitor offers Hindi, Tamil, or Telugu. We have Sarvam AI TTS integration.
  5. Social impact moat: Media coverage, awards, NGO partnerships create organic distribution.
  6. Technical readiness: YOLOv8, OCR, depth estimation all run on $4 chips today. The AI stack exists.

ADIP Scheme — How Users Get Devices FREE

The Assistance to Disabled Persons (ADIP) scheme is a Central Government program under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. It funds assistive devices for persons with disabilities who earn less than Rs 20,000/month. The scheme operates through authorized implementation agencies — primarily ALIMCO (Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India) and empaneled NGOs.

1.5 Drone Voice Control Opportunity

India's drone market is projected to grow from Rs 1,800 Cr (2024) to Rs 12,000+ Cr by 2030, driven by agriculture, infrastructure inspection, and logistics. The government's PLI scheme for drones and the liberalized Drone Rules 2021 have created a favorable regulatory environment. Over 200 Indian drone startups have emerged — but none offer natural language voice control.

Why Voice for Drones? Current drone operation requires a physical remote control with 12+ buttons and 2 joysticks. Farmers in fields, photographers at weddings, and inspectors on towers need their hands free. Voice commands like "take off, go to the mango trees, spray for 5 minutes, come back" are natural. Our intent engine already understands Hindi voice commands from the OmniPilot app — we just need to translate them to MAVLink protocol.
Business Model Insight: We don't build drones. We build the intelligence layer. License the voice SDK to Garuda Aerospace (India's largest drone manufacturer, 2000+ drones), IoTechWorld (agriculture drones), and ideaForge (defense). Per-device license fee + cloud subscription for AI processing. Zero hardware risk, pure software margins.

Drone Voice Control — No Direct Competitors

There are no voice-controlled drone platforms available today — not in India, not globally. DJI offers gesture control (hand signals) but not natural language voice commands. This is a greenfield opportunity. The closest analog is DJI's Smart Controller (Rs 1.5L) which has a touchscreen but no voice AI. Our SDK can add voice control to any MAVLink drone for Rs 8,999 — that includes the BLE hardware adapter + 1-year cloud subscription.

Competitive Risk: DJI could add voice control to their ecosystem. However, DJI drones are banned for government use in India (Chinese company), and most Indian agricultural drones use MAVLink-compatible flight controllers (Pixhawk, Cube). Our India-first, MAVLink-first approach is defensible. Garuda Aerospace, India's largest drone company, uses Pixhawk — ideal for our SDK.
Moat Analysis: Our true competitive moat is not technology (YOLO and OCR are open-source) but distribution + language + price. ADIP scheme access, NGO partnerships (NAB has 700+ chapters), Hindi/Tamil/Telugu TTS, and a Rs 5K price point create a combination no imported product can match. Building this moat requires relationships, not just code.
Phase 1 — Strategy

1.7 Risks & Mitigation Strategies

#RiskSeverityLikelihoodImpactMitigation
1 Cloud dependency
Device useless without internet		 High High 60% of blind users in rural India have spotty connectivity. Scene description, OCR correction, and TTS all need cloud. No internet = dumb camera. Lite tier (Rs 4,999) is fully offline. On-device YOLOv8n + PaddleOCR + eSpeak TTS. Cloud features are the premium tier (Rs 12,999). Offline mode handles 70% of daily needs: obstacle detection, currency ID, basic OCR.
2 ADIP empanelment delay
Government process takes 6-12 months		 High Medium If ADIP empanelment takes 12+ months, we miss the free-distribution channel. D2C sales to BPL population will be near-zero at Rs 5K. Parallel track: D2C sales to urban users (Rs 12,999 Standard) fund operations while ADIP empanelment is in progress. Partner with NAB (National Association for the Blind) who have existing ADIP relationships and can expedite the process.
3 BIS certification failure
Device fails EMC/safety testing		 Medium Low Cannot legally sell in India without BIS certification. Testing takes 6-8 weeks. Failure means redesign cycle of 2-3 months. Pre-compliance testing: Use ERTL Bangalore for preliminary EMC testing (Rs 50K) before formal BIS submission. Design with known-good reference circuits from ESP32-S3 design guides. Budget 2 certification attempts in timeline.
4 AI accuracy insufficient
Object detection misses critical objects		 High Medium False negatives (missing an obstacle) could cause injury. False positives (false alarms) erode trust. Blind users are physically dependent on accuracy. India-specific training data: Fine-tune YOLO on Indian objects (auto-rickshaws, open manholes, stray dogs, Indian currency). 3-month data collection sprint with 50 beta testers. Confidence threshold at 80% — only announce high-confidence detections. Always pair with audio-only obstacle warning (ultrasonic) as backup.
5 Smartphone dependency
30% of target users don't have smartphones		 Medium High Standard and Pro tiers need a companion smartphone for cloud AI processing. 70% of BPL visually impaired users may not own a smartphone. Lite tier is fully standalone — no smartphone needed. For Standard tier, explore JioPhone-style 4G module integration in a future version (adds $8 to BOM). Partner with Jio for bundled SIM with data plan optimized for AI queries (low bandwidth, API calls only).
Highest Risk Summary: The combination of cloud dependency + smartphone dependency + rural connectivity means the Lite offline tier is not just a budget option — it's the survival product. If we can't deliver a useful experience without internet and without a smartphone, we don't have a product for 80% of our target market. The Lite tier must be genuinely useful on its own.

The Fundamental Question: Can we build a Rs 4,999 device that genuinely improves a blind person's daily life? If the answer is yes — even if it only does obstacle detection + currency identification + basic Hindi OCR — the market and distribution will follow. Every risk above becomes manageable once we have a product that actually works for real users.

2.4 Certification & Regulatory Compliance

Required Certifications for India Market

CertAuthorityCost (INR)TimelineDetails & Requirements
BISBureau of Indian StandardsRs 1.5-2.5L6-8 weeksMandatory for electronic devices sold in India. IS 13252 (safety) + IS 616 (EMC). Requires product samples (8-10 units), factory audit for imported goods (waived for India mfg), annual surveillance. Lab: ERTL, STQC, or BIS-recognized lab.
WPCWireless Planning CommissionRs 50K-1L4-6 weeksRequired for WiFi + BLE radios. ESP32-S3 uses ISM 2.4GHz band. Apply for Equipment Type Approval (ETA). If using a pre-certified ESP32-S3 module (FCC/CE marked), WPC approval is simplified — modular certification applicable.
EMCSTQC / NABL labsRs 80K-1.5L4-6 weeksElectromagnetic Compatibility testing: conducted + radiated emissions, immunity tests. Part of BIS process but can be done separately for pre-compliance. Helps catch issues early before formal BIS submission.
BatteryBIS (IS 16046:2018)Rs 50K-80K4-6 weeksLiPo battery must comply with IS 16046 (derived from IEC 62133). Requires UN38.3 transport testing if batteries shipped separately. Most LiPo pouch cells from reputed suppliers come pre-certified.
SARTEC (Telecom Eng. Centre)Rs 30K-50K2-3 weeksSpecific Absorption Rate testing for devices worn on body. Required because pendant is worn on chest. BLE power is very low (max 10mW), so SAR is well within limits. Quick approval expected.

Certification Strategy

Parallel processing is the key to meeting the 3-4 month timeline:

  1. Week 1-2: Pre-compliance EMC testing at ERTL Bangalore (Rs 50K) — catches design issues early
  2. Week 2-3: Fix any EMC issues found in pre-compliance
  3. Week 3: Submit BIS application + WPC application + Battery test simultaneously
  4. Week 4-8: BIS testing (6 weeks) + WPC testing (4 weeks) + Battery testing (4 weeks) run in parallel
  5. Week 6-8: SAR testing (2 weeks) — can start while BIS is in progress
  6. Week 8-12: Receive all certifications, apply BIS mark to product, update packaging
Pro Tip: Using a pre-certified ESP32-S3 module (which already has FCC and CE certification) significantly simplifies the WPC process. Espressif provides all RF test reports and compliance documents. The WPC approval becomes a paperwork exercise rather than a full testing cycle, saving 2-3 weeks and Rs 50K+ in testing costs.

Growth Flywheel

The OmniPilot Growth Engine:
Impact Stories (blind user testimonials) drive Media Coverage (newspapers, TV, YouTube) which drives NGO Partnerships (NAB, Sightsavers) which drive ADIP Empanelment (government orders) which creates Volume (lower BOM cost) which enables Lower Prices which creates more Impact Stories.

This flywheel is self-reinforcing. The first 50 genuine testimonials from blind users are the fuel that starts it spinning. Everything else follows from real impact.

Phase 3 — Product Design

3.1 Blind Assistive Device Architecture

Think of it this way: A pendant with a camera (eyes), a microphone (ears), a speaker (voice), and a vibration motor (touch). The AI running on the phone is the brain. The camera sees the world, the AI understands it, and the speaker describes it in your language. It's like having a sighted friend who constantly tells you what's around you.

Component Architecture

ComponentHardwareFunctionLatencyProcessing Location
CameraOV5640 5MP, autofocusCaptures scene at 5-15fps depending on mode<50ms captureOn-device (ESP32-S3 captures frame)
Object DetectionESP32-S3 + NPU assistYOLOv8-nano detects people, vehicles, obstacles, animals<100msOn-device (quantized INT8 model)
Depth EstimationMiDaS v3 smallMonocular depth map for obstacle proximity warning<200msPhone (via BLE) or cloud
OCRPaddleOCRReads text in Hindi, English, Tamil, Telugu + 5 more<300msOn-device (Lite) or phone (Standard)
Scene DescriptionLLM (GPT-4o mini / Gemma)"You are at a crossroad. There's a bus stop on the left with 3 people waiting."1-3sCloud only (Standard/Pro tier)
Currency IDCustom CNN (3 layers)Identifies Indian currency notes (Rs 10 to Rs 2000)<50msOn-device (embedded model, 200KB)
Face RecognitionFaceNet / ArcFace liteRecognizes saved faces (family, friends). "Mom is 2 meters ahead."<500msPhone (via BLE) — Pro tier only
NavigationPhone GPS + DepthTurn-by-turn walking directions with obstacle avoidanceContinuousPhone + cloud (Google Maps API)
Hindi TTSSarvam AI / eSpeakConverts AI output to natural Hindi speech<200msSarvam cloud (Standard) / eSpeak on-device (Lite)
Haptic FeedbackVibration motor 10mmProximity warnings: faster vibration = closer obstacle<10msOn-device (direct GPIO)

Data Flow: What Happens When User Presses the Button

  1. User double-taps pendant → ESP32-S3 wakes camera
  2. Camera captures frame → 640x480 JPEG, ~30KB
  3. On-device YOLO runs → Detects objects, bounding boxes (100ms)
  4. If text detected → PaddleOCR reads Hindi/English text (300ms)
  5. If currency detected → CNN identifies denomination (50ms)
  6. Lite tier stops here → eSpeak announces "Person ahead, 2 meters. Sign reads: Dr. Sharma Clinic." (total: 500ms)
  7. Standard tier continues → Image sent to phone via BLE (200ms) → phone sends to cloud LLM
  8. Cloud LLM generates scene → "You're standing in front of a medical clinic. The sign says Dr. Sharma in Devanagari. There are two people sitting on a bench to your left." (1-2s)
  9. Sarvam AI converts to Hindi speech → Natural Hindi voice plays through earpiece
The 500ms Promise: For the Lite tier (offline), the total pipeline from button press to speech output is under 500ms. That's fast enough to feel instant. The Standard tier adds 2-3 seconds for the rich scene description but always plays the basic detection first so the user isn't waiting in silence.

Build Path: App First, Hardware Second

Smart Sequencing:
  1. Month 1: Build the AI pipeline as an Android app. Phone camera = eyes. Phone speaker = voice. This validates the AI stack with zero hardware risk.
  2. Month 2: Give app to 20 blind beta users. Collect feedback: what features matter most, what accuracy is needed, what form factor they want.
  3. Month 3: Design pendant hardware based on validated app experience. Only build the hardware features that beta users actually use daily.
This "app-first" approach means we never build hardware features nobody wants. The app is the prototype; the pendant is the product.

Phase 3 — Product Design

3.4 Drone Voice Integration Architecture

Command Taxonomy

Command TypeExample (English)Example (Hindi)Processing
Direct"Take off""Ud jao"1:1 mapping to MAVLink command. No parameters needed. Instant execution.
Parametric"Go up 10 meters""Das meter upar jao"Extract numeric parameter + direction. Map to MAVLink altitude change.
Semantic"Orbit the building""Building ke around ghoom"Requires GPS context + object detection. Plan circular waypoint mission around detected structure.
Contextual"Go to where you were before""Pehle wali jagah pe jao"Requires session memory. Recall previous waypoint and navigate back.
Mission"Spray my field starting from the northeast corner""Uttar-purv kone se khet mein spray karo"Complex: parse field boundaries from GPS, plan spray pattern, calculate pesticide flow rate. Multi-step mission.

Safety Architecture (6 Layers)

#Safety LayerWhat It DoesOverride Behavior
1GeofencePrevents drone from flying beyond pre-set GPS boundaries. Auto-return if breached.Cannot be overridden by voice. Hard limit. Only changeable via app settings with PIN.
2Command WhitelistOnly recognized commands execute. Unknown voice input is rejected with "Command not recognized."Prevents hallucinated or misheard commands from executing. Whitelist is version-controlled.
3Confirmation GateDangerous commands require verbal confirmation: "Confirm: fly to 120 meters altitude?"Timeout = abort. "Cancel" = abort. Only "Confirm" or "Haan" proceeds.
4Dead Man's SwitchIf no voice/BLE contact for 30 seconds, drone hovers in place. 60 seconds = auto-return-to-launch.Prevents flyaway if operator loses connection. Timer resets on any valid voice input.
5Battery GuardAuto-return-to-launch when battery hits 25%. Warning at 35%. No takeoff below 40%.Cannot be overridden. "I need 5 more minutes" is rejected if battery is critical.
6Airspace CheckQueries Digital Sky / AirMap API before takeoff. Blocks flight in no-fly zones (airports, military).Cannot be overridden. Required by DGCA. Displays zone info: "You are 2km from airport. Flight not permitted."

Partner Strategy: SDK Licensing, Not Building Drones

PartnerTypeTheir DronesOur IntegrationRevenue Model
Garuda AerospaceMfg (India's largest)Kisan Drone (agri), TSAW deliveryVoice SDK on their GCS + BLE adapter for field opsRs 8,999/drone/year + setup fee
IoTechWorldAgri drone specialistAgribot, Kissan DroneHindi voice commands for farmers ("Spray shuru karo")Rs 8,999/drone/year
ideaForgeDefense/enterpriseNinja, Switch, NetraEnglish voice commands for surveillance operatorsEnterprise license Rs 2-5L/year
DJI (via resellers)Consumer/prosumerMavic, Mini, Air seriesApp-based voice control (no hardware adapter needed)App subscription Rs 999/year
We Don't Build Drones. We build the intelligence layer. Garuda has manufacturing, distribution, and service networks across India. They don't have AI voice control. We have AI voice control. We don't have drone manufacturing. Partnership > vertical integration. This keeps our CAPEX near zero for the drone vertical.

The Platform Play

The Amazon Echo Playbook: Amazon launched Echo as a $180 speaker in 2014. Today there are 20+ Echo devices across every room in the house — from the Echo Dot ($30) to Echo Show ($250) to Ring cameras ($100) to Blink ($30). The speaker was the beachhead. The ecosystem is the business.

OmniPilot's beachhead is the blind assistive pendant. The ecosystem is: pendant + drone adapter + smart home + vehicle + health + security. Each device shares the same AI platform, same app, same voice interface. Users who buy one device are pre-sold on the next one because the experience is seamless.

Government Strategy

Government BodyProgramValue to UsAction Required
ALIMCOADIP Device EmpanelmentFree distribution to 100K+ users/yearSubmit device specs + pricing + test reports. Present at ALIMCO board meeting. Provide 10 evaluation units.
DGCADrone Type CertificationLegal requirement for drone SDK salesSDK partners (Garuda) handle drone certification. We provide voice control documentation for their safety case.
GeM PortalGovernment eMarketplaceDirect government procurementRegister as seller on GeM. List blind assistive device. Respond to ADIP tenders from state disability departments.
BIRACBIG Grant (Rs 50L)Non-dilutive development fundingSubmit Phase I application with prototype + beta data. If approved, Phase II for scale-up.
DSTPRAYAS Grant (Rs 10L)Hardware prototyping fundingApply through incubator (THub or CIIE). Need incubator endorsement letter.
Startup IndiaDPIIT Recognition + Seed FundTax benefits + Rs 50L seedAlready DPIIT registered. Apply for Seed Fund through approved incubator.
Government Relationship Playbook:
  1. Start with NGOs, not government directly. NAB has existing ADIP relationships. They introduce us to ALIMCO. Going directly to ALIMCO as an unknown startup is a 12-month process. Via NAB, it's 6 months.
  2. Build evidence first. Government bodies want proof: beta test data, user testimonials, working prototypes. Our 90-day plan generates all of this before any government engagement.
  3. Use grants strategically. BIRAC BIG funds development. ADIP funds distribution. Startup India Seed funds operations. Stack these — they're not mutually exclusive.
The NAB Multiplier: One successful demo at a NAB chapter leads to invitations from 10 more chapters. NAB's annual convention attracts 500+ delegates from across India. A 5-minute demo at the convention could generate 50+ partnership leads, 10+ bulk order inquiries, and media coverage in disability-focused publications. This single event could be our biggest marketing moment of Year 1.

This is About Impact.

Every number on this page represents a real person. 1,000 devices in Year 1 means 1,000 people who can now read their medicine labels, identify currency notes, navigate streets safely, and describe the world around them — in their own language.

The business case is strong: 60%+ margins, multiple revenue streams, government funding. But the real measure of success is simpler:

1 device = 1 person who can see through AI.

If we build something genuinely useful for 50 people in the first 3 months, the rest will follow. Impact is the engine. Revenue is the exhaust.

Scale Economics: At 10,000 units, our landed cost drops to Rs 1,480/unit. At the D2C price of Rs 12,999, that's 88.6% gross margin. Even at ADIP pricing of Rs 4,500, margin improves to 67.1%. The business gets dramatically better at scale. The first 500 units are about proving the product; units 501-10,000 are about building the business.
